terms.prefLabel: One TypeScript conformance suite for both libraries
terms.definition: suite.ts: 45 checks over every interface of the `hcert` world, type-checked (tsc, toolchain/node) against api/generated/ts, the TypeScript jco derives from the WIT contract, and driven by the shared vectors. run.mjs runs it against the Kotlin/JS package (hcert-core's WitJs facade) or the jco-transpiled Rust component; each loader only regroups its package's exports under the interface names. Both must pass (STT-TST-007). cross.mjs loads both and runs cross.ts: each library verifies the other's ES256 and PS256 certificates, built from byte-identical Sig_structures (STT-TST-003, STT-GEN-006).
Fetch the DVCMin logical models as FHIR R5 StructureDefinitions from the smart-trust-phw build at the commit models/fhir/SOURCE.yaml pins, into models/fhir/.

Run the HL7 FHIR Validator (validator_cli.jar) on the StructureDefinitions in models/fhir against the FHIR version they declare, with the jar and every FHIR package pinned by sha256 in toolchain/fhir-validator/validator.json, verified before use, and no fetch at run time (-no-http-access, -tx n/a). The site's pre step: it runs when the site is published to main and says it is not run for a staging preview.

terms.prefLabel: TypeScript declarations from the WIT contract
terms.definition: Run jco over api/wit to write the TypeScript view of the contract into api/generated/ts, the API reference that Node and browser callers read. jco comes from the pinned toolchain/node lockfile, installed with scripts disabled.

The Kotlin implementation of the HCERT pipeline and Verifiable Health Links, for the JVM (Android as-is) and Node: `hcert-api`, the declarations wit2kotlin generates from the WIT contract, and `hcert-core`, the behaviour (deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256, ZLIB, Base45, HC1, the trust list, verification, the VHL payload, the ITI-YY5 manifest request and JWE dir/A256GCM). No third-party runtime dependency; every build artefact is pinned in gradle/verification-metadata.xml.

The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the `hcert` world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). Every crate is pinned in Cargo.lock (DEPENDENCIES.md).

terms.prefLabel: Payload models from the FHIR logical models
terms.definition: Derive, from the FHIR logical models in models/fhir, the JSON-LD context, SHACL shapes and CDDL rules in models/generated/ that the payload codecs and the conformance checks read.

Derive vectors/negative/negative-vectors.json from the smart-trust PR 129 certificates: one language-neutral file of inputs a conforming verifier must refuse, each with the step and reason it must stop at. The Kotlin suite, the Node smoke test and the Rust suite load the same file. Nothing is newly signed: each case changes a byte, a prefix, the clock or the trust list.

Assemble the two npm packages of the libraries, @litlfred/hcert-component (the jco-transpiled Rust component) and @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js (the Kotlin/JS library), from their build outputs, each with a package.json that has the VERSION, no dependencies and no scripts; and check that VERSION, the single version source, is a semantic version that Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, the Gradle build, CHANGELOG.md and every built package.json and POM agree with. The Maven dry run is the hcert-kotlin build's publishDryRun task and the crate's is cargo package; docs/RELEASING.md is the runbook an agent follows to publish.

terms.prefLabel: Every test has a Gherkin Scenario
terms.definition: Check test/features/*.feature against the suites: every Rust #[test], Kotlin @Test and TypeScript conformance run(...) has a Scenario tagged @test:<path>::<test>, every such tag names a test, WHO-ITB Scenarios carry @itb:<suite>/<testcase>, and every test-plan case names its feature file. Temporary, until cat-harness check:test-gherkin is pinned.

Write test/plans/hcert-library-conformance.test-plan.json (test-plan/v1) from the skills and the requirements' success criteria: one case per skill, one assertion per criterion verified by test. The plan any implementation of the library, Kotlin or Rust, runs.

terms.prefLabel: Systems under test and their bindings
terms.definition: Write the bindings and uncovered lists of each test/systems/<id>.system.json (system/v1) from the tags in its tests: the requirement ids a Kotlin, Rust or TypeScript test's name starts with, or a script's "Verifies" sentence. Each assertion of a plan the system claims gets the tests that verify it, with the surface and target each runs on; each required assertion a declared target leaves unverified, and no `unbound` entry explains, is listed as uncovered.

Make vectors/ihe-vhl/jwe-dir-a256gcm.json with node:crypto alone, so the library's RFC 7516 dir / A256GCM decryption (with and without zip DEF) is checked against an implementation that is not the library. TEST ONLY: the key is in the file.

terms.prefLabel: Kotlin skeleton from the WIT contract
terms.definition: Generate the Kotlin declarations in tools/hcert-kotlin/hcert-api from api/wit by fixed mapping rules: records to data classes, variants to sealed interfaces, resources to AutoCloseable interfaces, result<T, E> to HcertResult; worlds are not generated, and no Kotlin name or KDoc mentions WIT.
